test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 21 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants to / crack the upcoming deal.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issue in the sentence lies in the phrase "**knuckle up really seriously**."
 
• The phrase "knuckle up" is not the correct idiomatic expression. The appropriate phrase is "**knuckle down**," which means to work hard or focus seriously on a task.
 
• Additionally, using "**really seriously**" creates redundancy, as both words convey a similar meaning. One of them should be omitted for clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He will have to knuckle down seriously if he wants to crack the upcoming deal."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "He will have to"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "if he wants to"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 1: "crack the upcoming deal."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.
